items.headline: NFL chief medical officer: Eagles' approach to Hurts was 'appropriately guarded'
items.description: At the owners meetings Tuesday in New York, NFL officials staunchly defended the process involving Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and his blood clot issue, with chief medical officer Allen Sills addressing reporters in a media availability.

items.headline: Reports: NFL won't punish Eagles for letting Jalen Hurts play with blood clot
items.description: The NFL will not punish the Eagles for how they handled the process surrounding quarterback Jalen Hurts being cleared to play Week 5 against the Jaguars, according to multiple reports.
